question: Does a fighter's age cost the same at every weight, and for an elite UFC record as for any other? (asked 2026-10-24: heavyweights, and perhaps the lighter divisions, may age later)

candidates.division_curves: each division its own knee and slope (age_div), chosen on FIT by the log loss of that division's bouts alone: knee with the shared slope, then slope, then knee again, divisions in the order listed, each on top of the ones before; a division with fewer than min_fit_bouts FIT bouts with both ages keeps the shared curve
candidates.division_knees: each division its own knee, the shared slope (-15), chosen the same way
candidates.elite: age_elite_slope (more Elo per year past the knee for a fighter with 6+ UFC wins at 70%+ before the bout), chosen on FIT over every bout
candidates.division_curves_and_elite: division_curves, then the elite slope chosen on FIT on top of them

keep_rule: SELECT log loss at least 0.0005 below 1.2.0's and FIT no worse; among the kept, the lowest SELECT log loss
promote_rule: TEST log loss at least 0.0005 below 1.2.0's on the same bouts with the card-blocked paired 95% interval below zero, and the Brier score no worse
disclosure: Written 2026-10-24 before any candidate was fitted. Already seen, on every bout since 2016 (FIT, SELECT and TEST): 1.2.0's error for the older fighter by division and age, and for older fighters with an elite UFC record (6+ wins at 70%+, the cut-off used here). A heavyweight-only later knee (0-6 years) was tried on all three windows and made each worse; it is not a candidate. TEST was read for 1.2.0's promotion; this is the first read for an age-by-division model.
